h1: The 7 Best Garden Auger Drill Bits Under $100 for Bulbs, Beds and Seedlings, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Garden Auger Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 garden auger drill bits priced under $100, from single bulb bits to a 5 set, compared on diameter, length and drill fit.
summary: The TCBWFY 1.6 and 3.5 inch two-bit set is the garden auger to buy for most gardens, and the K-Brands 2 pack is its closest rival. The 5 Set is the pick if you want a bit for every job, the MAXCCINO 2 inch covers mid-size holes, and the single 1.6 inch bits suit bulb-only planting. All of them cost far less than $100.
intro: A $100 budget for a garden auger is a trap, because it implies a lot of money buys a lot of auger. It does not. Every product in this ranking costs between nothing much and about $50, and spending more than that does not make a bit dig better. The real choice is which diameters you need, how long the bit must be and whether your drill can drive it. Money left over is better spent on a good drill with a clutch.

We reviewed eight auger drill bits, set aside the shorter K-Brands 4 by 12 inch, and ranked seven by diameter range, length, number of bits in the pack and compatibility with a standard hex drive. Listings give no material grade, so we note that gap. Price buckets replace exact prices. The ranking is research-based and nothing in it comes from trying the bits in a garden.

products.name: TCBWFY Garden Auger Drill Bit for Planting 1.6"x16.5"and 3.5"x16",Heavy Duty Bulb Planter Tool for Digging Holes,Compatible with 3/8" Hex Drive Drill
products.verdict: A 1.6 inch bulb auger and a 3.5 inch planting auger together, both for a 3/8 inch hex drill.
products.description:
TCBWFY sells this pair of augers, a 1.6 by 16.5 inch bit and a 3.5 by 16 inch bit, both made for a 3/8 inch hex drive drill. The listing calls them heavy duty and sells them for under $25.

The pair covers the two jobs most gardeners actually do. Narrow holes take bulbs, garlic and small seedlings, and wider holes take pot-sized plants and perennials. Sixteen inches is deep enough for the usual planting depth in one pass. The wide bit needs good drill torque and slow speed, so a light drill may stall.

Buy it if you plant a mix of bulbs and bedding plants. Skip it if bulbs are all you plant, where a single narrow bit is enough.
cons: Wide bit needs a strong drill
products.idealFor: Gardeners planting bulbs and bigger starts.

products.name: K-Brands Auger Drill Bit for Planting 2 Pack 1.6" x 16" & 3.5" x 16" Set
products.verdict: Two 16 inch augers, 1.6 and 3.5 inches wide, from a brand that also sells single bits.
products.description:
K-Brands bundles a 1.6 by 16 inch auger and a 3.5 by 16 inch auger into one set, priced under $25. The listing offers no other details.

It competes head to head with the TCBWFY pair, since the sizes are nearly identical, and the half inch difference in the narrow bit's length is the only visible change. Two sizes mean you pick the hole for each plant instead of forcing every job through one bit. As with all augers in this price range, check that your drill has a 3/8 inch chuck and enough torque for the wide bit.

Buy it if you prefer a brand that sells each size separately for easy replacement. Skip it if you want a stated steel grade.
products.idealFor: Gardeners who want a matched pair.
products.skipIf: You want a stated steel grade.

products.name: 5 Set Auger Drill Bit for Planting, Heavy Duty Garden Auger Spiral Drill Bit Bulb Planter Tool for Planting Bedding Plants, Universal for Cordless Drill
products.verdict: A five-bit set for bedding plants and bulbs, described as universal for cordless drills.
products.description:
This five-bit set is sold as a heavy-duty garden auger collection for planting bedding plants and bulbs, universal for cordless drills, in the $25 to $50 bracket. The listing does not name the sizes.

Five bits is the most in this guide, and the point of a set is choosing a diameter for each plant, from small bulbs to larger pots. Variety is a strength for a keen gardener who plants widely. The risk is the missing size information and the brand, because without the actual diameters you cannot be sure the set includes what you need. A case or holder is not mentioned.

Buy it if you plant many kinds of things and want options. Check the sizes in the product images first.
cons: Sizes are not named in the title

products.name: MAXCCINO Auger Drill Bit for Planting 2"(D) x14.5(L), Garden Ground Earth Spiral Drill Bit for 3/8" Hex Drive Drill, for Post Hole Digger
products.verdict: A 2 inch by 14.5 inch bit between bulb size and shrub size, for a 3/8 inch hex drill.
products.description:
The MAXCCINO measures 2 inches across and 14.5 inches long, with a 3/8 inch hex shank, and costs under $25.

Two inches sits in the useful middle: too wide for tiny bulbs but a good fit for big bulbs, seedling plugs and small perennials, while asking for less torque than a 3.5 inch bit. The listing calls it a post hole digger, which stretches the truth, as two inches only holds thin stakes. It is a single size, so you will still want a second bit for other jobs.

Buy it if most of your planting falls in the mid-range. Skip it if you want one bit for tiny bulbs.
cons: Post digger wording is a stretch

products.name: TCBWFY Auger Drill Bit for Planting 1.6x16.5inch Extended Length Garden Auger Spiral Drill Bit for Planting Bulbs Flowers, Post Hole Digger
products.verdict: A single 1.6 by 16.5 inch bulb bit for 3/8 inch hex drills, under $25.
products.description:
This TCBWFY bit is the lone narrow auger, 1.6 inches wide and 16.5 inches long, made for a 3/8 inch hex drive drill and listed for bulbs and flowers.

A bulb-only gardener does not need the pair, and a single narrow bit asks little of the drill. The 16.5 inch length lets you reach planting depth in one pass without bending over. Its limits are plain: it makes one hole size, and the post hole digger claim in the title is not realistic at this diameter.

Buy it if you plant tulips, daffodils and garlic and nothing wider. Move up to the two-bit set if you plant anything bigger.

products.name: SORANGEUN Auger Drill Bit for Planting - 1.6" x 16.5" Plant Auger for Cordless Drill - Bulb Planter Tool for Bulbs Planting&Holes Digging
products.verdict: A 1.6 by 16.5 inch plant auger described for cordless drills.
products.description:
The SORANGEUN is a 1.6 by 16.5 inch plant auger written for cordless drills, costing under $25. The listing offers no further specifications.

It matches the TCBWFY single bit on size, so the decision hangs on trust. A narrow auger is a simple object, but good ones have clean welds on the spiral and a straight shaft, neither of which can be checked from a listing. Cordless drills with a clutch pair well with this size.

Buy it if it undercuts the TCBWFY on the day. Otherwise take the better documented bit.
products.skipIf: You want proof of build quality.

products.name: Garden Auger Drill Bit for Planting 1.6" x 16.5" -3/8" Hex Drive Compatible
products.verdict: An unbranded 1.6 by 16.5 inch bit, compatible with a 3/8 inch hex drive.
products.description:
This generic garden auger is 1.6 inches wide and 16.5 inches long and fits a 3/8 inch hex drive. It has no brand and no further details, and costs under $25.

It ends the list because it matches the same size as two ranked bits with less backing. A throwaway bit can still do the job of making a few dozen bulb holes in loose soil. In stony or heavy ground, a weak weld or thin steel will show quickly.

Buy it for a one-off bulb planting day. For a bit you will use every season, pay a little more for a named maker.
products.skipIf: You dig every season in hard soil.

whatMatters.detail: Diameter decides what you can plant. 1.6 inches handles bulbs and garlic, 2 inches handles large bulbs and plugs, and 3.5 inches handles pot-sized plants. A wide bit asks much more of the drill, so match diameter to drill power.
A longer bit reaches planting depth in one pass but flexes more and wanders in stony soil. Fourteen to sixteen and a half inches is typical. Start the hole slowly and let the flutes bring soil up.
All the bits here use a 3/8 inch hex shank, which most cordless drill chucks accept. Check your chuck opens that wide. Using an impact driver is not recommended unless the maker allows it.
Roots and stones can seize an auger and twist the drill. A clutch or low-speed setting limits the kick. A side handle on the drill gives you leverage against the twist.
A set gives choice, while a single bit gives focus. A five-bit set suits a varied garden, but only if it names the sizes. Otherwise a pair of well-chosen diameters does more.

faq.q: Do I need a special drill for a garden auger?
faq.a: No. Any drill whose chuck accepts a 3/8 inch hex shank will do. A cordless drill with a clutch and a low-speed setting is best, and wide bits ask for more torque.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with garden augers?
faq.a: Pushing too hard at high speed. Let the flutes lift soil, back the bit out often and slow down near roots. Forcing it can twist your wrist or burn out a small drill.

faq.q: Is a pair worth it over a single bit?
faq.a: For most gardens, yes. A 1.6 inch bit handles bulbs and a 3.5 inch bit handles larger plants. A single bit is enough if you only plant bulbs.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Push the hex shank fully into the chuck, tighten it, and start on a low speed. Mark the depth on the bit with tape if you need consistent planting depth.

faq.q: How do I keep augers from rusting?
faq.a: Brush off soil, wipe dry, and store indoors, ideally with a light coat of oil. Soil moisture rusts bare steel quickly.

faq.q: Can I use them in hard clay?
faq.a: They can work in moist clay at low speed. Dry, stony ground is tough and may stall the drill, so water the spot first and clear the bit often.

finalTake: For most gardens, the TCBWFY 1.6 and 3.5 inch pair is the best garden auger under $100, with the K-Brands pair a close second. The 5 Set is the choice for a varied garden if it lists its sizes, and the MAXCCINO covers mid-size holes. Spend your leftover budget on a drill with a clutch, not on a pricier bit.
